newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: MANILA'S NAPOCOR OKAYS PACT WITH KEPCO.
newsitem.headline: MANILA'S NAPOCOR OKAYS PACT WITH KEPCO.

text.p: The Philippines' National Power Corp (Napocor) said on Wednesday its board had approved an energy conversion agreement with Korea Electric Power Corp (Kepco).
Under the agreement, Kepco will build a 1,200-megawatt gas-fired power plant in Ilijan, Batangas, south of Manila.
In return, Napocor will pay Kepco a monthly capital recovery fee of $7.25376 per kilowatt-hour aside from fixed operating and maintenance fees and an energy fee, Napocor said in a statement.
The agreement with Kepco will hasten talks on a gas supply pact between developers of the Camago-Malampaya gas field - Shell Philipines Exploration B.V. and Occidental Petroleum Inc - and Napocor.
Shell Philippines is a unit of the Royal Dutch/Shell group while Occidental Philippines Inc is a subsidiary of Occidental Petroleum Corp.

The natural gas that will be used to run the Ilijan power plant will be sourced from the Camago-Malampaya field in southwest Philippines. The Ilijan power plant is scheduled to start operation in January 2002.
